column3: Occurrence or prevention of harm associated with healthcare delivery, such as healthcare-associated infections, medication-related adverse events and other potentially preventable complications.
column5: AHRQ, 2023 NHQDR, Appendix B: Patient Safety measures

column3: Ability to obtain medical care when a need arises, including unmet need or delayed care. Focuses on obtaining care rather than having insurance or a regular provider.
column5:
ODPHP, Healthy People 2030, AHS-04: Access to needed medical care;
CDC/NCHS, Healthcare Access and Quality, Data Query System.

column3: Having health insurance during a specified reference period, including coverage type or gaps when relevant. Coverage does not imply that needed services are accessible or affordable.
column5: ODPHP, Healthy People 2030, AHS-01: Health insurance coverage

column3: Care that respects individual needs, preferences and values, including understandable communication, respectful treatment and involvement in decisions. Focuses on the care experience rather than adverse events.
column5:
AHRQ, National Healthcare Quality and Disparities Report: framework and data tools
AHRQ, 2025 NCEPCR Annual Report: Person-Centered Care

column3: Receipt of recommended preventive services, such as screening, counseling and immunization, among people for whom those services are indicated.
column5: ODPHP, Healthy People 2030, AHS-08: Recommended preventive health care

column3: Having a regular place or provider used when sick or seeking health advice. Refers to an ongoing care connection, rather than whether a particular episode of needed care was obtained.
column5: ODPHP, Healthy People 2030, AHS-07: Usual source of care

column3: Financial ability to obtain healthcare, including care delayed or forgone because of cost and the burden of out-of-pocket expenses. Insurance ownership is a separate outcome.
column5:
CDC/NCHS, Healthcare Access and Quality, Data Query System;
AHRQ, National Healthcare Quality and Disparities Report: framework and data tools.

column3: A person's classification as employed, unemployed or outside the labor force at a reference time. Describes labor-market position rather than selection by a particular employer.
column5: BLS, Current Population Survey: Concepts and Definitions

column3: Availability and receipt of employer-provided nonwage benefits, such as health insurance, retirement plans and paid leave. Excludes wages and individually requested accommodations.
Being employed or actively seeking and available for work under the applicable statistical definition. The participation rate is the labor force as a share of the relevant population.
column5: BLS, Current Population Survey: Concepts and Definitions

column3: Monetary compensation for work, measured on a specified hourly, weekly or annual basis. Distinguishes pay levels from nonwage benefits and satisfaction with pay.
Progression to higher positions, responsibilities or pay grades within a career, including promotion opportunities and realized promotions. Excludes initial hiring.
column5: EEOC, Know Your Rights: Workplace Discrimination is Illegal; Pew Research Center, How Americans View Their Jobs (2023).

column3: Ability to request and obtain adjustments needed to apply for or perform a job, such as changes to equipment, schedules or communication. Distinguishes individualized adjustments from general employee benefits.
column5: EEOC, Know Your Rights: Workplace Discrimination is Illegal

column3: Exposure to unwelcome verbal, physical or other conduct in the workplace, including identity-related hostility or intimidation. Distinct from hiring, pay and promotion decisions.
column5:
EEOC, Know Your Rights: Workplace Discrimination is Illegal;
Williams Institute, LGBTQ People's Experiences of Workplace Discrimination and Harassment 2023 (2024 report).

column3: Continued employment with the same employer over a defined interval, or separation through dismissal or layoff. Distinguishes continuity of a job from being employed somewhere at one time.
column5:
EEOC, Know Your Rights: Workplace Discrimination is Illegal;
BLS, Employee Tenure: statistical tables.

column3: Selection into a job, including progression to an offer or employment following an application. Focuses on entry decisions rather than current employment status or later promotion.
column5:
EEOC, Know Your Rights: Workplace Discrimination is Illegal;
Pew Research Center, How Americans View Their Jobs (2023).

column3: Opportunity to enroll in and participate in education at the relevant level. Focuses on entry to educational provision; selective college admission and advanced-course placement are separately specified stages.
column5:
U.S. Department of Education/OCR, Access to Equal Educational Opportunity;
U.S. Department of Education, 2021-22 CRDC: A First Look (2025).

column3: Highest educational level or credential already completed by a person at the reference date. Describes accumulated education rather than completion within a specific entering cohort.
column5: U.S. Census Bureau, Educational Attainment in the United States: 2024 tables

column3: Entry to postsecondary education, with application, admission and initial enrollment treated as distinct stages. Admission refers specifically to an institution's decision on an application.
column5:
NCES, IPEDS Survey Methodology: Admissions, Graduation Rates and Fall Enrollment components;
U.S. Department of Education/OCR, Access to Equal Educational Opportunity.

column3: Achievement in an identified subject and educational level, measured using assessments or course results. Focuses on demonstrated learning rather than enrollment, credentials or persistence.
column5: NCES, NAEP: Scale Scores and Achievement Levels

column3: Opportunity to enroll and actual enrollment in advanced or accelerated courses, such as Advanced Placement or advanced mathematics. Course availability and student participation are separate measures.
column5: U.S. Department of Education, 2021-22 CRDC: A First Look (2025)

column3: Exposure to formal school disciplinary actions, such as suspensions, expulsions or referrals to law enforcement. Focuses on institutional sanctions rather than peer harassment.
column5: U.S. Department of Education, 2021-22 CRDC: A First Look (2025)

column3: Continued enrollment toward completion across consecutive periods. Retention means return to the same institution; persistence can include continued study elsewhere. Does not mean grade repetition.
column5:
NCES, IPEDS Fall Enrollment component: retention rates;
NCES, IPEDS Survey Methodology: Admissions, Graduation Rates and Fall Enrollment components.

column3: Exposure to harassment or bullying in an educational setting, including conduct related to identity. Focuses on victimization experiences or reported incidents rather than the entire school climate.
column5: U.S. Department of Education, 2021-22 CRDC: A First Look (2025)

column3: Completion of a specified educational program or credential within a defined period among an identified starting cohort. Distinct from highest lifetime attainment.
column5:
NCES, Measuring Student Success in IPEDS: GR, GR200 and OM;
NCES, IPEDS Survey Methodology: Admissions, Graduation Rates and Fall Enrollment components.

column3: Conditions immediately surrounding a dwelling, such as noise, litter, perceived safety and satisfaction with the neighborhood. Excludes defects inside the unit and access to an individual public service.
column5:
U.S. Census Bureau, AHS Table Creator Release Notes: housing and neighborhood measures;
U.S. Census Bureau, 2023 AHS Topical Content Variable Reference File.

column3: Ability to find and secure a dwelling in the rental or purchase market, including opportunities to receive information, view units and obtain an offer. Distinct from cost burden or existing ownership.
column5: HUD, Housing Discrimination Against Racial and Ethnic Minorities 2012 (2013 report)

column3: Ability to obtain rental housing, including responses to inquiries, opportunities to view available units and leasing decisions. This is the rental-market subtype of access to housing.
column5:
HUD, Housing Discrimination Against Racial and Ethnic Minorities 2012 (2013 report);
HUD, Paired-Testing Pilot Study of Housing Discrimination Against Same-Sex Couples and Transgender Individuals.

column3: Ability to maintain an ongoing place to live over time, including payment difficulties, forced moves or insecure tenure. Eviction is a specific pathway to instability; homelessness is a distinct housing state.
column5:
U.S. Census Bureau, 2023 AHS Topical Content Variable Reference File;
U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 Household Pulse Survey, Cycle 06: housing payment and eviction-likelihood tables.

column3: Living in an owner-occupied dwelling or holding ownership, as defined by the measure. Describes housing tenure rather than approval of a mortgage or opportunities during housing search.
column5: U.S. Census Bureau, Housing Vacancies and Homeownership: Homeownership Rates

column3: Housing costs relative to household resources, typically measured through rent or owner-cost burdens. Distinct from physical housing conditions and continuity of residence.
column5:
HUD, Worst Case Housing Needs: 2025 Report to Congress (2023 AHS data);
U.S. Census Bureau, About the American Housing Survey.

column3: Physical condition and habitability of a dwelling, including structural, plumbing, heating and other adequacy problems. Excludes surrounding-neighborhood conditions and cost burden.
column5:
U.S. Census Bureau, About the American Housing Survey;
HUD, Worst Case Housing Needs: 2025 Report to Congress (2023 AHS data).

column3: Lacking a fixed, regular and adequate nighttime residence under the selected operational definition. Measures may distinguish sheltered and unsheltered situations and point-in-time versus annual experience.
column5: HUD, 2024 Annual Homelessness Assessment Report, Part 1: Point-in-Time Estimates

column3: Threat or perceived likelihood of losing a rented dwelling through eviction within a stated time horizon. Distinct from completed eviction, general financial strain and homelessness.
column5:
U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 Household Pulse Survey, Cycle 06: housing payment and eviction-likelihood tables;
U.S. Census Bureau, 2023 AHS Topical Content Variable Reference File.

column3: Ability to obtain borrowing when needed, including unmet credit demand and barriers that prevent an application. Broader than the lender's approval decision among submitted applications.
column5: Federal Reserve, Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households in 2025: Credit (2026 report)

column3: A numerical estimate of repayment risk derived from credit-report information using a specified scoring model. Distinct from the lender's broader underwriting decision and from having a scoreable credit record.
column5: CFPB, What is a credit score?

column3: Whether a person has a credit record and whether the available history is sufficient to generate a score. Distinguishes no record from an existing but unscoreable record and from a low score.
column5: CFPB, Technical correction and update to the credit invisibles estimate (2025)

column3: A lender's decision to approve, partially approve or deny a submitted credit application. Specify the credit product and applicants as the relevant population.
column5:
Federal Reserve, Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households in 2025: Credit (2026 report);
CFPB, Summary of 2023 Data on Mortgage Lending (HMDA).

column3: Approval or denial of an application for a home mortgage within a specified loan category. This is the mortgage-specific subtype of credit/loan approval.
column5: CFPB, Summary of 2023 Data on Mortgage Lending (HMDA)

column3: Ability to obtain and use bank or credit-union services, including barriers related to cost, location, account requirements or trust. Ownership of an account is a distinct realized outcome.
column5: FDIC, 2023 National Survey of Unbanked and Underbanked Households

column3: Having a checking or savings account at a bank or credit union at the reference date. Distinguishes banked from unbanked status rather than ease of accessing or using services.
column5: FDIC, 2023 National Survey of Unbanked and Underbanked Households

column3: Use of nonbank transaction services such as check cashing, money orders or remittances. For this matrix, excludes borrowing products covered under mainstream vs alternative credit use.
column5: FDIC, 2023 National Survey of Unbanked and Underbanked Households

column3: Price and contractual conditions of offered or originated credit, including interest, fees, loan amount and repayment terms. Distinct from whether the application was approved.
column5: CFPB, Summary of 2023 Data on Mortgage Lending (HMDA)

column3: Use of bank or credit-union credit compared with nonbank borrowing products such as payday, pawn, auto-title or rent-to-own credit. Restricted to borrowing products.
column5: FDIC, 2023 National Survey of Unbanked and Underbanked Households

column3: Being arrested or held in police custody during an encounter or investigation. Excludes a court's subsequent pretrial detention decision and imprisonment after conviction.
column5:
BJS, Police-Public Contact Survey: methodology and questionnaires
BJS, Federal Justice Statistics, 2023 (March 2025)

column3: Decisions about whether to prosecute a referred matter and which charges to pursue or dismiss. Distinct from police arrest and the court's determination of guilt.
column5:
BJS, Federal Justice Statistics Program: case-processing framework;
BJS, Federal Justice Statistics, 2023 (March 2025).

column3: Whether an accused person remains in custody or is released while the case is pending, including conditions of release. Distinct from police custody at arrest and punishment following conviction.
Being confined in a jail or prison during a specified period or reference date. Distinguish the number currently confined from admissions, time served and sentencing decisions.
column5:
BJS, Correctional Populations in the United States, 2023: Statistical Tables;
U.S. Sentencing Commission, Individuals in the Federal Bureau of Prisons.

column3: An encounter initiated by police, including approaches, traffic or street stops and arrests. Refers to whether and how contact begins rather than the outcome of a later court process.
column5: BJS, Police-Public Contact Survey: methodology and questionnaires

column3: Disposition of a criminal case, including conviction, acquittal or dismissal, with pleas and trials distinguished when relevant. Excludes sentence type and duration.
column5:
BJS, Felony Defendants in Large Urban Counties, 2009: Statistical Tables (2013);
BJS, Federal Justice Statistics, 2023 (March 2025).

column3: Being subject to community correctional supervision, distinguishing probation from post-prison parole or other release supervision. Excludes confinement in jail or prison.
column5: BJS, Correctional Populations in the United States, 2023: Statistical Tables

column3: Type and severity of the sanction imposed after conviction, including imprisonment, probation and sentence length. Distinct from case disposition and the stock of people incarcerated.
column5:
U.S. Sentencing Commission, 2025 Federal Sentencing Statistics;
BJS, Felony Defendants in Large Urban Counties, 2009: Statistical Tables (2013).

column3: Being stopped by police while driving, riding in a vehicle or in a public place, with the encounter type specified. A narrower subtype of police-initiated contact.
column5: BJS, Police-Public Contact Survey: methodology and questionnaires

column3: Experience of threatened or actual physical force by police during an encounter, with type and severity specified. Distinct from contact or arrest alone.
column5: BJS, Police-Public Contact Survey: methodology and questionnaires

column3: Actual enrollment in or receipt of benefits from a named program during a defined period. Distinct from eligibility and approval without subsequent receipt.
column5:
U.S. Census Bureau, Survey of Income and Program Participation;
SSA, SSI Annual Statistical Report, 2024.

column5:
SSA, SSI Annual Statistical Report, 2024: Outcomes of Applications for Disability Benefits;
CMS, Medicaid and CHIP Eligibility Operations and Enrollment Snapshot.

column3: Ability of an eligible person to navigate the process and obtain an available benefit. An umbrella construct spanning information, application and receipt; these stages are separately defined below.
column5:
GAO, Administrative Burden: OMB Should Update Instructions to Help Agency Assessment Efforts (GAO-25-107239, 2025);
U.S. Census Bureau, Survey of Income and Program Participation.

column3: Meeting a named benefit program's substantive eligibility criteria at a specified time, such as income, resources, age or disability requirements. Distinct from knowing the rules, applying or being awarded a benefit. Rules differ across programs and cannot be transferred between programs.

column3: Knowledge that a benefit exists and understanding of its basic eligibility rules and application route. Distinct from actually meeting eligibility criteria or receiving a benefit.
column5: GAO, Administrative Burden: OMB Should Update Instructions to Help Agency Assessment Efforts (GAO-25-107239, 2025)

column3: Continuation of an existing benefit through redetermination or renewal, including termination or interruption. Distinct from the outcome of an initial application. Rules differ across programs and cannot be transferred between programs.
column5:
CMS, Medicaid and CHIP Eligibility Operations and Enrollment Snapshot;
SSA, SSI Annual Statistical Report, 2024.

column3: Elapsed time from application submission to an eligibility or award decision. Excludes the interval from approval to first payment, which requires a different measure. Rules differ across programs and cannot be transferred between programs.
column5:
CMS, Medicaid MAGI and CHIP Application Processing Time Report;
CMS, Medicaid and CHIP Eligibility Operations and Enrollment Snapshot.

column3: Time, effort and psychological costs required to learn about, apply for or retain a benefit. Distinguishes the burden imposed by the process from eligibility or its final decision.
